text:
Marco: quick heads-up — private VPC workloads on small GPU slices (4g.1x) are seeing a regression after yesterday's kernel selector change. p95 token latency for short-chat flows jumped ~1.8x, throughput dip ~12%. KV cache hit rate reported dropping from ~92% to ~68% :grimacing:

Li: ugh. is this definitely the kernel selector or something in the batching heuristics? any perf traces/sketches?

Marco: initial traces look like more frequent kernel fallbacks to fp32 on tiled ops, plus more small batches forming (many 1-2 request batches). KV metrics show increased cache misses correlated with those tiny batches.

perf-bot: deploy-note: kernel-selector v2.14 rolled to private region us-west-2 at 11:12 UTC yesterday (canary -> 60%). rollback window closed.

Li: can you paste the flame output or the scheduler snapshot? even a sampled trace helps.

Marco: pasted simplified snippet (sampling):
```
flame: time(ms):
  batch_collect: 18 -> 36 (median)
  kernel_select: 2 -> 9
  run_kernel(fp16): 6 -> 22 (fallback to fp32 in ~30% of runs)
kv_cache.lookup: hit 92% -> 68% (spike of 404ms miss penalty)
```

Marco: repro: run 1k short-chat requests (avg 18 tokens generated) on 4g.1x slice with kv_cache enabled and token_budget=48.

Anuj: sounds like two coupled things: kernel selector prefers int8/quantized kernels but due to sequence-length distribution and small batches it ends up picking incompatible kernels and falling back. That fallback plus extra per-batch overhead is killing small-request latency.

Eva: do we have a metric for how often the batching window produces suboptimal groups? maybe our batch formation thresholds are too aggressive for private slices with low concurrency.

Ryan: agree. private hardware often has constrained memory so our default max_batch_tokens * token_budget combo can make us flush early. For small GPUs we should allow higher token_budget or increase batch_timeout_ms to let more docs join.

Anuj: quick config override we can add to private profiles to test (put in customer private config as experiment):
```
private.batch_overrides:
  max_batch_tokens: 6144  # allow larger token aggregations
  token_budget: 128       # favor grouping more short chats
  batch_timeout_ms: 30    # a bit more waiting to reduce 1-2 sized batches
  queue_priority: [interactive, background]
  kernel_selection.prefer_fp16: true
  kernel_selection.fallback_threshold_ms: 5
```

Li: two immediate experiments: 1) force older kernel-selector v2.13 on canary slice to confirm regression source, 2) apply Anuj's private.batch_overrides on a small subset of customers to see hit/loss tradeoff.

perf-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eng-runtime/kernel-fallbacks (note: access restricted).

Marco: I rolled a manual canary to v2.13 on one private slice — latency back to baseline there. Positive signal.

Eva: good signal. can someone compute delta in KV hit-rate when batching knobs changed? need to ensure increased batch_timeout doesn't cause undue latency for high-priority interactive requests.

Ryan: we can do a hybrid policy: if request.priority == interactive, keep batch_timeout_ms=10, else bump to 30. also track token_budget per-priority.

Anuj: add a queue-policy prototype: FIFO for interactive up to token_budget=48; opportunistic coalesce for background with token_budget=128. Quick pseudo: 
```
if priority == "interactive":
  token_budget=48
  batch_timeout=10
else:
  token_budget=128
  batch_timeout=30
```

Li: also instrument kernel_select.remote_reason tag so we can see why selector chooses fallback (memory/shape/quant mismatch). add telemetry to traces.

Marco: I'll add that telemetry + repro harness to run against the private canary slice. putting together a PR for rollback + selective overrides in config.

Eva: test matrix: (v2.13, v2.14) x (default knobs, Anuj overrides) x (interactive/concurrent loads). I can help run it tomorrow morning.

Ryan: owners: Marco -> repro + rollback PR; Li -> telemetry + selector logs; Anuj -> override config + deploy script; Eva -> test runs & result aggregation.

Marco: thanks — will post short summary + numbers once I have the canary run. tagging @ryan and @eva to sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
